entities.name: Philipp von Hutten
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Philipp von Hutten was a German adventurer and an early European explorer and conquistador of Venezuela, who played a significant role in the history of Klein-Venedig, the concession of Venezuela Province to the Welser banking family by Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor and King of Spain.

 Born in the early 16th century, von Hutten joined the Spanish Empire's conquest of South America and traveled to Venezuela in 1528, where he served as a governor and helped establish trade routes. His expeditions led to the discovery of new resources, including gold and silver, which significantly contributed to the growth of the Spanish Empire.

 The legacy of Philipp von Hutten can be seen in the development of Venezuela's economy and its integration into the global trade network. His contributions also had a lasting impact on the history of the region, shaping its cultural and political landscape.

 The final words of Philipp von Hutten remain a testament to his enduring legacy, as he wrote, 'I have conquered a great part of the New World, and have made my fortune, but I have not found the treasure I sought.'
